study.notes: STUDY: open label randomised trial (Guangzhou, Obesity Medicine 2017) in overweight or obese Chinese women with PCOS: exenatide 10 ug twice daily (dose_mg 0.01 per injection) vs metformin 1000 mg twice daily, 41 per arm randomised by a computer generated system, 63 completed (31 exenatide, 32 metformin, Table 2 n), 12 weeks (the eligibility minimum); Table 2 gives baseline and after therapy mean plus or minus SD per arm with time and interaction p values (route arm_change_imputed_r, correlation 0.5); weight is the primary outcome, metabolic and endocrine parameters are secondary (prespecified TRUE); pct_weight_change from the Table 2 means in the exenatide arm, 71.84 to 66.64 kg, minus 5.20 kg equals minus 7.2 percent (metformin 72.04 to 68.49 kg, minus 4.9 percent; interaction p 0.009); funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, no conflicts (industry_funded FALSE); population PCOS with overweight or obesity, held under amendment A6; rob_overall high

rows.notes: Table 2: triglycerides mmol/L, exenatide vs metformin, NS
Table 2: total cholesterol mmol/L; interaction p below 0.001 (metformin fell more)
Table 2: fasting blood glucose mmol/L, NS
Table 2: fasting insulin mU/L; interaction p below 0.001 as printed
Table 2: HOMA-IR; time p below 0.001, interaction p 0.004
Table 2: hsCRP mg/L; time p below 0.001, interaction p 0.016

json.design: open label randomised trial, exenatide 10 ug twice daily vs metformin, overweight or obese women with PCOS, 82 randomised, 63 completed, 12 weeks
json.reason: population polycystic ovary syndrome with overweight or obesity, held under amendment A6 (Director decision on held populations); seven inventory markers extracted to staging from Table 2 by the imputed change route
other_markers: 2 h glucose and insulin, glucose and insulin AUC, insulin sensitivity index
testosterone, free androgen index, SHBG, LH, DHEAS
menstrual frequency, modified Ferriman Gallwey score

rob.justification: computer generated allocation without concealment described (D1 some concerns); open label (D2 some concerns); 19 of 82 did not complete, completers analysed (D3 high); laboratory assays (D4 low); no registration cited, outcomes named in the methods (D5 some concerns)

doubts: held population (PCOS); 23 percent attrition with completers analysed
the same first author and setting as group 202 (ChiCTR-IIR-16008084, 2017) but a different trial (82 vs 176 randomised, Obesity Medicine vs the 2017 journal of group 202); treated as a separate trial
